title: Measurement and units
lede: The metric system, the prefixes that make it easy, and the difference between accurate and precise.

sections.md:
## The SI system
Science worldwide uses the **International System of Units (SI)**, the modern metric system. Seven base units define everything else:

| Quantity | Unit | Symbol |
|---|---|---|
| Length | meter | m |
| Mass | kilogram | kg |
| Time | second | s |
| Temperature | kelvin | K |
| Electric current | ampere | A |
| Amount of substance | mole | mol |
| Light intensity | candela | cd |

## Prefixes do the heavy lifting
Every metric unit scales by powers of 10, using the same prefixes:

| Prefix | Symbol | Means |
|---|---|---|
| mega | M | 1,000,000 |
| kilo | k | 1,000 |
| centi | c | 1/100 |
| milli | m | 1/1,000 |
| micro | μ | 1/1,000,000 |

So 1 kilometer = 1,000 meters, 1 milligram = 1/1,000 of a gram. To convert, just move the decimal.

sections.md:
## Accuracy vs precision
- **Accurate:** close to the true value.
- **Precise:** repeated measurements are close to each other.

A scale that always reads 2 lb heavy is precise but not accurate. Good measurement needs both. That's why trucks get weighed on certified scales.

sections.label: Useful conversions
sections.md: 1 inch = 2.54 cm (exactly). 1 mile ≈ 1.609 km. 1 kg ≈ 2.205 lb. 1 gallon ≈ 3.785 liters.
